APPROVE
`Next` now scores about 11 (the loop, four `if`s with their nesting, and two boolean-operator sequences), and each extracted helper does exactly what the inlined code did, including the same `k`, `isDefault`, name, endpoint and URL values. The one thing I couldn't check is the build: the repository isn't on this machine, so I couldn't confirm that `Span` is the actual type returned by `f.FunctionBodyAfter(k)`, the only spot where the patch could fail to compile.
